title: Experiment 1: Does watching an NPC change how the agent learns to survive?
setup: Every agent sees two grids side by side: its own, and a second one with its own fire and food that it can never enter. In the first group the second grid is empty. In the other two an NPC lives on it, moving around and eating; its state (health and energy) is hidden in one and visible in the other, drawn on the same channels as the agent's own. The agent and the NPC never interact, and the NPC's state never enters the agent's reward. Everything else uses the default settings, and every run trains for 200k environment steps with Double DQN and a store of past deaths in every batch (against catastrophic forgetting).

metrics.pushes: Pushes of the NPC per episode
metrics.npc_fire_steps: NPC steps on fire per episode
metrics.npc_survival: NPC alive when the episode ended (fraction)
metrics.buffer_terminal_share: Buffer: share of transitions that are deaths
metrics.action_gap: Action gap (max Q − min Q) on random-play states
metrics.doomed_q_error: Doomed states: max Q minus true value

questions.title: Does watching the NPC help the agent, and does seeing its state help more?
questions.short: Watching the NPC: higher reliability and fewer starvation deaths; no clear difference in fire deaths. Reliability: 85% against 66%. Seeing the NPC's state: no clear difference in reliability and starvation deaths and fire deaths. Reliability: 94% against 85%.
answer: Watching the NPC: higher reliability and fewer starvation deaths; no clear difference in fire deaths. Reliability: 85% trained with the NPC, state hidden, 66% trained without the NPC (+18 points; 95% interval +9 to +28; p = 0.024). Starvation deaths per 1,000 test episodes: 32 against 58 (−27; 95% interval −46 to −10; p = 0.032). Fire deaths per 1,000 test episodes: 0.2 against 0.0 (+0.2; 95% interval 0.0 to +0.7; p = 1.000).

Seeing the NPC's state: no clear difference in reliability and starvation deaths and fire deaths. Reliability: 94% trained with the NPC, state visible, 85% trained with the NPC, state hidden (+9 points; 95% interval −5 to +20; p = 0.317). Starvation deaths per 1,000 test episodes: 20 against 32 (−12; 95% interval −30 to +11; p = 0.365). Fire deaths per 1,000 test episodes: 0.7 against 0.2 (+0.5; 95% interval −0.5 to +2.2; p = 1.000).

questions.title: Is the agent learning to survive, or does it depend on what it sees of the NPC?
questions.short: Watching the NPC: no sign that survival depends on it at test time, but the final networks alone can't confirm a learned gain. Seeing the NPC's state: no sign that survival depends on it at test time, but the final networks alone can't confirm a learned gain.
answer: Watching the NPC: no sign that survival depends on it at test time, but the final networks alone can't confirm a learned gain. Agents trained with the NPC, state hidden, tested without the NPC instead: 0.97, against 0.98 tested as trained (−0.01; 95% interval −0.02 to −0.01; p = 0.062). Tested in the same setting (without the NPC): 0.97 trained with the NPC, state hidden, 0.97 trained without the NPC (0.00; 95% interval −0.02 to +0.02; p = 0.937).

Seeing the NPC's state: no sign that survival depends on it at test time, but the final networks alone can't confirm a learned gain. Agents trained with the NPC, state visible, tested with the NPC, state hidden instead: 0.98, against 0.98 tested as trained (−0.01; 95% interval −0.02 to +0.01; p = 0.438). Tested in the same setting (with the NPC, state hidden): 0.98 trained with the NPC, state visible, 0.98 trained with the NPC, state hidden (0.00; 95% interval −0.02 to +0.02; p = 0.897).

questions.title: Why? Candidate explanations

hypotheses.name: Shared features
hypotheses.idea: The NPC's body appears on the same channels as the agent's. Watching it get hungry, walk to food and eat trains the convolutional features the agent also uses for its own body.
hypotheses.prediction: The advantage needs the NPC on the shared body channel: an NPC drawn on a channel of its own should not help.
tests: Train with the NPC on a separate channel (new setting).

hypotheses.name: Moving input
hypotheses.idea: A moving NPC keeps the picture changing from step to step, which may stop a greedy agent from getting stuck repeating the same moves. That would help it without it learning anything about the NPC.
hypotheses.prediction: The advantage shows only while the NPC is there (section 2), and an NPC that moves at random without eating helps just as much.
tests: Train with an NPC that wanders at random and never eats (new setting).

questions.short: Not tested yet. Candidates: shared features and moving input.
